title: Provisioning Gatekeeper: Safety Buffer Allocator and Approval Journey
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers requesting dedicated capacity often ask for aggressive throughput guarantees without an empirical headroom budget, leading to either operator over-provisioning (wasted cost) or under-provisioning (SLO breaches). Current intake screens capture committed RPS and token estimates but do not provide an algorithmic safety buffer recommendation tied to autoscaling policies, fleet controls, and expected burst profiles. Goal: Build a 'Provisioning Gatekeeper' that (1) simulates near-term demand variability based on submitted workload patterns, (2) recommends a safety buffer in throughput units and autoscale policy knobs (min/max replicas, cool-downs), and (3) wires into the approval lane with a transparent justification for sales/solutions and for finance approvals.
proposal: Deliver a 3-part flow: (A) Intake enrichment and simulator: extend intake form to capture peak-percentiles, warm-start behavior, and KV cache hit expectations; run a Monte Carlo-ish simulator that outputs 95/99th percentile token/sec and KV cache pressure. (B) Safety Buffer Allocator: compute a recommended buffer (a headroom multiplier and an absolute token/sec buffer) that maps to fleet sizing and latency SLO probability. Provide a 'conservative' and 'economy' mode. (C) Approval Journey: surface the simulator results and chosen buffer in the provisioning UI and generate a succinct approval rationale and SLA contract language. Include an override path with required justification and linked mitigations (rate limits, fallback model variants).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form extended to collect peak-percentiles, warm-start time, KV cache hit rate assumption, and burst duration (UI + API)
Simulator runs on submitted intake and produces 50/95/99th percentile token/sec and expected KV cache pressure within 30s for typical requests
Allocator outputs a recommended buffer and maps to autoscale knobs (min_replicas, max_replicas, scale_cooldown_seconds) with justification text
Approval UI shows simulator graphs, buffer rationale, cost delta estimate, and an approval button that records approver + justification
Integration tests exist for simulator determinism and for end-to-end approval flow (intake -> simulate -> recommend -> approve)
All user-facing language reviewed and signed off by Solutions Eng and Finance for commercial wording

decisions: Use a probabilistic simulator (sampling-based) rather than closed-form assuming non-normal burst patterns
Expose both a conservative and economy buffer recommendation to allow negotiation during approval
Allocator will produce both absolute token/sec and a multiplicative headroom factor to map to different pricing models
Approval overrides allowed but must include mitigation checklist and senior approver sign-off
